summary: Tenga Rinpoche was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar. He studied at Benchen Monastery under Tai Situ Rinpoche, founded Benchen Monastery in 1976, and served as Dorje Lopön at Rumtek Monastery circa 1967–1980.

Tensei Kitabatake worked in Buddhist studies after studying at Ryukoku University (circa 1950–1955). He held multiple posts at Ryukoku University, including professor (1970) and president (1995–1999), and later served as president of Gifu Shotoku Gakuen University (1999–2005).
Tenshin Tanouye was active in Buddhist studies and religious studies. He studied under Sogen Omori and founded Chozen-ji.
Tenzin is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned a Master of Philosophy at the University of Oslo under the supervision of Hanna Havnevik, attested in 2008.

Tenzin Dorjee worked in Buddhist studies and Tibetology, studying under Geshes Lobsang Tsephel, Sonam Rinchen, and Dawa. He served as a translator at the Library of Tibetan Works and Archives and General Secretary at Pullahari Monastery (attested 2000).

Tenzin Gyatso is active in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He studied under teachers including Tsenshab Serkong Rinpoche, Trijang Lobsang Yeshe Tenzin Gyatso, Khunu Lama Tenzin Gyaltsen, and Dilgo Khyentse, and founded the International Network of Engaged Buddhists in 1989.

Tenzin L. Mullin specializes in religious studies and Buddhist studies. He completed a Master of Arts at the University of Otago, where he studied under supervisors Erica Baffelli and Elizabeth Guthrie.

Tenzin Namdak worked in Tibetology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. He studied under sGangs ru Tshul khrims rgyal mtshan, Lobpön Tsultrim Gyaltsen, and Shes rab bstan 'dzin rgyal mtshan, earned a degree at Menri Monastery, and founded Triten Norbutse Monastery.

Tenzin Wangyal Rinpoche specializes in Tibetology, religious studies, and philosophy. He studied at Menri Monastery and under teachers including Tenzin Namdak, directed the Dialectic School of Menri Monastery, worked at the Library of Tibetan Works and Archives, and founded Ligmincha International.

Ter Ellingson is a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He studied at Concordia College, the University of Chicago, and the University of Wisconsin–Madison, and served on the faculty at the University of Washington from 1981 to 2016.

Terese Tse Bartholomew specializes in history, archaeology, Tibetology, and sinology. She earned an M.A. from the University of California, Los Angeles, and served as Curator of Himalayan Art and Chinese Decorative Art at the Asian Art Museum of San Francisco.
Tertön Sogyal studied under Patrul Rinpoche and Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso, and he taught the 13th Dalai Lama.

Teruji Ishizu was a religious studies and philosophy scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1923–1926). He served as president of Tohoku University (1963–1966) and Miyagi University of Education (1965), and held professorships at Keio and Komazawa Universities.

Tessa J. Bartholomeusz was a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who earned degrees from the University of Florida, Florida State University, and the University of Virginia. She taught at Indiana University Indianapolis (~1991–2001) and Florida State University (1993).
Tessa Verney Wheeler was a scholar in history and archaeology. She was educated at Addey and Stanhope School from 1905 to 1911 and studied at University College London from 1911 to 1914.

Tetsuei Sato was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Ryukoku University (~1925–1931). He served as a professor at Taisho University and Gifu Keizai University (~1971), and became professor emeritus at Ryukoku University (~1971–1982).
Tetsuhiko Shibata is a scholar of Buddhist studies who studied at Taisho University under teachers Eijun Hattori, Yukan Ozawa, and Mitsuo Sato.

Tetsujiro Inoue was a philosopher and religious studies scholar educated at the University of Tokyo, Heidelberg, and Leipzig. He served as professor and dean at the University of Tokyo, as well as president of Daito Bunka University (1925).

Tetsuo Otani is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Waseda University and Komazawa University. He served as president of Komazawa University (2002–2006), board chair at Tsuru University (2013–2016), and president of Tohoku Fukushi University (2015–2019).

Tetsuro Noguchi was a scholar of sinology, history and archaeology, and religious studies. He held posts at Yokohama National University (~1967–1976), the University of Tsukuba (~1976–1996), and J. F. Oberlin University (~1996–2003).
